answer.summary: At Lovable, high agency means spotting what needs doing, figuring it out, and owning it through completion—even beyond one’s specialty. sections.heading: High agency and autonomy in practice
sections.content: Verna says Lovable screens for both. A person should be able to handle work tangential to their role without waiting for a specialist—for example, a marketer launching something can figure it out themselves—and take ownership from start to finish. On the autonomy side, people have very little ground-level supervision and can choose what they work on, while still aligning around shared goals and major launches. They are enabled to try things; with the company’s velocity, a failed attempt is not treated as a big deal, and the team can pivot.
